name: Taniya Gill
project: Rooted in Our Land: A Visual Toolkit on Native Plants and Climate Adaptation
deck: Thirty-five people, three workshops, ten native species and a journal each to keep. The smallest project in the cohort, and the only one that made room for Delhi’s queer community in the same room as the schoolchildren.
description: Three nature journaling workshops in Delhi, ten native species observed and a journal each to keep. Children, students, artists, the queer community.

aims.h: Draw it and you notice it
aims.p: Nature journaling as an observation method rather than an art class. A leaf you have drawn once is a leaf you can name in the street.

aims.h: Walk the city you already live in
aims.p: Guided tree walks through Delhi green spaces, watching which animal visits which plant and in what week.

aims.h: Ask the people who do not get asked
aims.p: Children, students, artists and members of the queer community, in the same workshop and on the same walk.

did: Ran three nature journaling workshops in community spaces and parks
Led guided tree walks through Delhi green spaces
Recorded plant and animal interactions and seasonal patterns with participants
Gave every participant a nature journal to keep
Began an infographic zine on the native plants of Delhi

quotes.text: I had never really noticed the details of leaves before this workshop. Drawing them helped me slow down and observe things I usually ignore.
quotes.speaker: An undergraduate student

quotes.text: This was my first time attending a tree walk, and I really enjoyed learning about native plants through drawing.
quotes.speaker: A workshop participant

quotes.text: It was fun experiencing drawing the trees of Delhi. The last time I painted was when I was in school
quotes.speaker: A workshop participant

quotes.text: I really appreciate your work. The kids really enjoyed and learned from the experience
quotes.speaker: A session incharge

holes: The zine is the thing the project was for, and it was not finished when the report closed. It was due on 25 April 2026 and there is no copy here yet.
Every testimonial is anonymous. That was the design of the workshops, not an omission.
